chapters.title: Genesis 1
body: Before anything else is said about God, this is said so gently: he speaks, and there is light. The world begins "without form, and void" — empty, unshaped, waiting — and God doesn't rush in to force it right. He simply speaks, softly and surely, into the emptiness, and order begins to unfold, one quiet day at a time: light, then sky, then land, then life.

That's the pattern he offers you, too. If today feels unformed — a decision still unmade, a relationship still tender, a plan still coming together — you don't have to have it figured out first. God is already there with you, speaking gently into the unfinished places, patient and unhurried, already calling what's forming good.
